Megiddo
meh-GID-doh
proper noun
Hebrew Megiddo, perhaps “place of troops” or “rendezvous,” a fortress city commanding the great plain of Esdraelon.

See also: Megiddo

📖 Biblical Definition

Megiddo was a fortress city of the half-tribe of Manasseh, set where the pass opens upon the great plain of Esdraelon, the highway of armies between Egypt and the north. It was a town Manasseh held but did not cleanse of its Canaanites (Jos 17:11). Its plain was a famous field of battle from the days of the judges, when the kings of Canaan fought in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo (Jdg 5:19). There Josiah, the last good king of Judah, would not turn from his rash war against Pharaoh-nechoh, but came to fight in the valley of Megiddo, and was slain (2Ki 23:29; 2Ch 35:22), so that the plain became the place of Judah’s deepest mourning. From this storied field of slaughter the Spirit took a name for the last great conflict of the age, gathering the kings of the earth to a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon, the hill of Megiddo (Rev 16:16). The dictionary marks Megiddo as the battlefield of the ages. Where the chariots of the heathen and the body of a godly king alike went down, the prophetic word sets the figure of the final overthrow of all the powers gathered against the Lord and against His Christ.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

A fortress city on the plain of Esdraelon, a famous field of battle and the root of the name Armageddon.

MEGIDDO, a fortress city commanding the great plain of Esdraelon.

It was a town of Manasseh, held but not cleansed of its Canaanites.

Its plain was a famous battlefield from the days of the judges.

There Josiah king of Judah was slain in battle against Pharaoh-nechoh.

From it comes Armageddon, the hill of Megiddo, the field of the last conflict.

📖 Key Scripture

2Ki 23:29 — "In his days Pharaohnechoh king of Egypt went up against the king of Assyria to the river Euphrates: and king Josiah went against him; and he slew him at Megiddo, when he had seen him."

Jdg 5:19 — "The kings came and fought, then fought the kings of Canaan in Taanach by the waters of Megiddo; they took no gain of money."

2Ch 35:22 — "Nevertheless Josiah would not turn his face from him, but disguised himself, that he might fight with him, and hearkened not unto the words of Necho from the mouth of God, and came to fight in the valley of Megiddo."

Rev 16:16 — "And he gathered them together into a place called in the Hebrew tongue Armageddon."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

A place of Scripture, not a contested doctrine; its storied battlefield gives the figure of the last great conflict.

expand to see more

Megiddo has met no redefinition from the present age, though its derived name Armageddon is much abused in loose and sensational talk. The dictionary records the city and its plain that the reader may know the field whose name the Spirit took for the final overthrow of the powers of darkness.

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the certainty of the last great judgment. The plain of Megiddo, drenched in the blood of Canaan’s kings and of godly Josiah, becomes in the prophetic word the figure of the day when the kings of the earth are gathered against the Lord and His Christ, and are overthrown. The believer reads in this ancient battlefield the pledge that every power arrayed against God shall fall at last upon the field of His appointing.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Hebrew perhaps “place of troops,” Megiddo names the fortress that gives Armageddon its name.
